But could be overfitting; the rule generative: noise = random zeros, plus the shape stamped multiple times in zeros. Output stamps 8s over all copies.

Hmm wait, but with chance copies at 28% density, false positives would occur in output too — but we can't distinguish since output = rule applied. Risky but likely intended: this is the known ARC-style "find hidden stamp pattern" task? Actually the real generative rule might be: the shape was stamped in several places in zeros; output recolors those stamps. If we also stamp at chance coincidences, we add extra 8s → wrong.

Alternatively maybe the underlying rule: recolor zero to 8 if zero-cells match the shape pattern shifted... With only noise + stamp, can't be certain. But the exact-copy rule perfectly explains output: 63 changed = copies. Let me verify no kept zero is part of a "partial" copy adjacent... whatever.

Better check: in output, changed regions — do all changed cells belong to at least one full copy? Yes by construction. And no kept zero belongs to a full copy? Since copies = changed, any zero in a full copy would be changed; kept = not in any copy. Consistent.

But is the true rule "stamp copies of the shape", where in the generative process copies were placed deliberately (non-overlapping-ish) and chance matches are noise? For the test, chance matches at 8-cell shape with 25% zero density: 0.25^8 ≈ 1.5e-5 per position × ~180 positions ≈ 0.003. Negligible!
